utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-88/2-A, the Prosecutor versus Zdravko Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let me make sure that the audio equipment is working properly. Mr. Tolimir, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to greet all of those present, and I hope that these proceedings will evolve in accordance with God's will. And yes, thank you, I hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SVARC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Svarc. Did I pronounce your name correctly?

utterances.speaker: MS. SVARC
utterances.text: Svarc, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, I see that your legal advisor, Mr. Aleksandar Gajic, is here. He has, of course, a right of audience during status conferences. This was granted by an oral decision of the Pre-Appeal Judge at the Status Conference on 5 July 2013. Mr. Gajic, you are here? Mr. Gajic, can I have you confirm it for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. As you are aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal, and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes: First, it allows the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions; second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. The Status Conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. In the present case, the last Status Conference was held on 22 October 2014; thus, this Status Conference is taking place before the expiration of the 120-day period specified in Rule 65 bis (B). Today's Status Conference was scheduled by the Scheduling Order issued on 20 January 2015. Let me now inquire into Mr. Tolimir's health. If Mr. Tolimir wishes, this discussion can take place in closed session. Mr. Tolimir, any problems with your health, detention condition, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I did have some problems with my health. Four stents were built into my heart, and I would kindly ask the Presiding Judge to ask the Detention Unit for the medical documentation involved so that it could be sent both to the Chamber and to my lawyer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Registrar, would you please communicate this to the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir would like himself to have the report of the medical experts on his health condition following the insertion of the stents, and he authorises submission of that same report to the Bench. Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. Turning to the recent update -- the update of the case. The appeal hearing in this case took place, as you know, on the Wednesday, 12 November 2014. The Appeals Chamber is deliberating on a judgement. Currently we have no pending motions before us, and I would like now to ask the parties whether they have any issues that they would like to raise. At this time, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SVARC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Dominika Svarc, on behalf of the Prosecution, together with my colleague, Todd Schneider, and our Case Manager, Janet Stewart. The Prosecution has no issues to raise at this moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, Mr. Gajic? I see no issues to raise at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at this moment we have no issues to rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gajic. Since there are no other matters to be raised, I thank the parties for their attendance and thank the interpreters for their work and call the proceedings to a close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: at 3.07 p.m.
